children: November 25 (Renewables Now) - Indian wind turbine maker Suzlon Energy Ltd (BOM:532667) said today it has laid the foundation stone for a new 1-GW factory in the state of Tamil Nadu where it plans to manufacture turbine blades for its S175/5MW machines.

The smart blade production plant will be installed in the district of Thoothukudi and will make turbine blades with a length of up to 95 metres (312 feet) for the tallest and most powerful machines available in India. The site will be Suzlon’s third in Tamil Nadu, adding to its two facilities in Coimbatore.

The new plant, expected to create over 1,000 jobs in manufacturing, will use artificial intelligence (AI) and electricity solely from renewable energy sources. Set to benefit from its proximity to potential wind-rich sites, its operation will support the delivery of Suzlon’s roughly 6-GW order book. “It will enable us to manufacture longer blades with greater precision, consistency and quality, ensuring reliable deliveries and better execution for our customers,” said CEO Ajau Kapur.
The wind turbine maker has been present in Tamil Nadu since 2001 and has installed over 3 GW of capacity in the state.

title: Suzlon to build 1-GW smart blade factory in Tamil Nadu
